corpus.note: Maintainers' AI corpus at repo data/write-like-me: 46 machine-generated documents in six registers. ai-generated/: 30 documents (22 pieces plus one email thread in eight stage files; GPT, Claude Fable/Opus/Sonnet/Haiku, Gemini Pro/Flash/Thinking) across article, report, social, abstract and email — the corpus of the 2026-09-09 extraction. skills/: 16 snapshots of three of this repository's agent-written skills (write-like-me, agent-experience, skill-evals: SKILL.md and every reference, copied at commit 6685400 so that quotes stay verifiable), register docs, added 2026-10-07; written by Claude coding agents (Fable 5.1, earlier drafts Fable 5 and Opus 5; skill-evals by an unrecorded mid-2026 Claude model) under a maintainer's direction and edited across review rounds, hence marked co-authored. Vetting is provenance on the maintainers' word; `measure --vet` flags presentations_gemini (ai_vocabulary) and generating-code_gemini-thinking (label_lead) as Gemini-typical outliers and three docs files on the constructions they discuss; none dropped. Four of the docs files describe writing markers, so counters there also fire on quoted examples: counts stay as the script wrote them, affected rows say so, and no evidence quote is a mention. register_weights {article 4, docs 3, report 2, social 2, abstract 2, email 1}: article keeps the largest share (29%), docs the second (21%), so that neither the one co-authored email thread nor one model family's docs register (47% of the words) defines every rate; weights move `rate` only (db-schema.md). The 2026-10-07 extraction was a four-reader Phase A over the docs files, merged with the reviewed DB, recounted over all 46 documents, then trimmed to the rows that carry a machine tell: neutral statistics (bold, italic, sentence length, person, modals) and rows under 0.3/1k with no register above 60% spread were dropped, quotes capped at four per row. Judged rows are counted under written rules: imperative = one per run of two or more consecutive reader-addressed imperative sentences; repetition = one per anaphora run of three or more consecutive sentences or paragraph openers sharing a frame (question volleys and imperative runs go to their own rows); enthusiasm = one per email reply or social post that opens by praising or validating the previous message, or an exclamatory launch; closer-type = 1 per piece (per post or abstract in a multi-piece file) that ends on a punchline, title echo or call to action; fragment = one per verbless or subjectless prose sentence; candor-claim = one per sentence announcing the text's own honesty. Open items: prompt provenance (plainly- vs. style-prompted) and a second, independent email thread.
